metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] Connections near the max_connections limit
metadata.description: Alerts when open connections to a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance (database/network/connections) are at least 90% of its max_connections setting (database/mysql/max_connections) in every observed minute of the last 10 minutes, with at least 3 minutes observed. At 100%, MySQL refuses new connections with 'Too many connections'. connection_usage_pct is the latest value, computed like the Connection usage % panel. Requiring every observed minute ignores single spikes and the partly filled newest minute.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Per instance and minute: open connections and the max_connections setting (MAX collapses duplicate points)
| STATS c = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections`)),
        mx = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/max_connections`))
  BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
| EVAL minute_usage = CASE(mx > 0, TO_DOUBLE(c) / mx, NULL)
// Latest connections and max_connections (ignoring minutes where the metric is missing) and the lowest per-minute usage
| STATS connections = LAST(c, CASE(c IS NOT NULL, `@timestamp`, NULL)),
        max_connections = LAST(mx, CASE(mx IS NOT NULL, `@timestamp`, NULL)),
        lowest_usage = MIN(minute_usage),
        observed_minutes = COUNT(minute_usage)
  BY database_id

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL connections near max_connections

Open connections have stayed at 90% or more of `max_connections`. When the limit is reached, new clients get `Too many connections` errors.

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Detail**. Check *Connections vs max connections*, *Threads connected, running and cached* and *Connection attempts by outcome*.
2. A sudden jump right after a restart, failover or maintenance is a reconnect storm. A slow climb is usually a connection leak or pool growth (pool size × application replicas).
3. Many connections with few threads running means idle connections are holding slots. Check pool idle settings and `wait_timeout`.
4. Check whether failed connection attempts are rising (*Failed connection surge*), which means clients are already being refused.

### Actions
Fix leaks, cap pool sizes, add a pooler, or terminate idle sessions. Raise `max_connections` only if the tier has spare memory, because each connection costs memory.

### Tuning
Change `lowest_usage >= 0.9` to adjust the threshold.
